extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for DFG funding; DFG reviewers, review board members, and research administration staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and official criteria used by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) to assess and assure the quality of research funding proposals and the review process. Covers substantive evaluation criteria for proposals and procedural quality-assurance standards for peer review and decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality and originality of the project
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific quality, topicality and novelty of the proposed research; whether the project advances knowledge in its field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the clarity of research questions/hypotheses, the soundness of the conceptual approach, and the project’s potential to contribute original results or insights. Poorly justified or incremental projects are downgraded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness and rigor of the methodology and design
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether the proposed methods, experimental design, analytical approaches and work plan are suitable to achieve the stated objectives and are methodologically rigorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes assessment of methodology selection, statistical power/sample size considerations, reproducibility measures, contingency plans, and the viability of timelines and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and realism of goals, timetable and workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the aims, scope and schedule of the project are realistic given the resources, personnel and time requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether objectives are over-ambitious, whether milestones are achievable, and whether workload distribution among team members is balanced and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant(s)’ qualifications and track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the principal investigator(s) and key personnel with respect to expertise, prior achievements, publication record and suitability to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of previous major results, experience with the methods proposed, mentoring record (if applicable), and the capacity to lead the project. Special allowances may be considered for early-career researchers where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, innovation and scientific advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the proposal is innovative and departs from established approaches to provide new concepts, methods or insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers judge whether the project opens new research directions, uses novel techniques, or combines disciplines in novel ways; mere incremental development is less favorably rated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and adequacy of infrastructure, facilities and institutional environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the host institution provides the necessary infrastructure, equipment and environment to successfully carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes access to specialized instrumentation, technical support, collaborative facilities, and institutional commitments (e.g., lab space, release from teaching).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness and justification of requested resources and budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether the personnel, equipment, consumables and other requested funds are necessary and reasonable in relation to the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers check for cost-effectiveness and avoid overfunding; unclear or unjustified budget items may lead to reductions or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the extent and quality of interdisciplinary approaches or collaborative arrangements that strengthen the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good interdisciplinary projects clearly justify the need for multiple disciplines, define how integration will occur, and document effective collaboration structures and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internationality and cooperation with national/international partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Value added by international collaboration or cooperation with other institutions, and the adequacy of plans for exchange and partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether partners bring essential expertise/resources and whether collaboration arrangements (e.g., secondments) are well described and feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal relevance and potential for knowledge/technology transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, the proposal’s potential societal, economic, clinical or technological impact and plans for dissemination or transfer of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes outreach, stakeholder engagement, patenting/industry liaison plans, or plans to inform policy — evaluated insofar as they are relevant to the discipline and proposal aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical, legal and safety considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether ethical, legal, biosafety, animal welfare or data-protection issues have been identified and adequately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must demonstrate appropriate approvals, informed-consent procedures, data protection measures, and risk mitigation strategies where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data management and open access
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of plans for managing, storing and making research data and publications accessible in line with DFG policies on open access and data stewardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes data management plans, long-term storage, metadata standards, and justifications for any restrictions on sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of equal opportunity and gender aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposal accounts for gender-relevant aspects in research content, team composition and measures promoting equal opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess gender-sensitive research design (where relevant), and whether the application demonstrates measures to promote equality and family-compatibility in staffing and supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification and training of junior researchers and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of plans for supervising, training and integrating early-career researchers or doctoral students within the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes structured training, clear supervision arrangements, and opportunities for career development and independence for junior staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and transparency of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether aims, methods, expected results, and work packages are clearly and transparently described in the proposal text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-structured, concise, and comprehensible proposals facilitate fair assessment; vague or poorly written proposals impede evaluation and receive weaker ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of timelines, milestones and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposal defines concrete milestones and deliverables that allow monitoring of progress and achievement of objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realistic, measurable milestones and indicators strengthen the assessment of feasibility and project management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value for money / cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the expected scientific gains justify the requested funding and whether the proposed use of funds represents efficient use of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes scrutiny of high-cost items and whether the scope could be achieved with less funding or phased support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest management and reviewer independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural standard that reviewers must be independent and conflicts of interest identified and handled to ensure objective assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFG requires declaration and avoidance of conflicts; conflicted reviewers are excluded from evaluation and panels must document recusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and qualification of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality-assurance criterion that reviewers appointed must have appropriate expertise and qualifications to appraise the proposal fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFG selects experts with subject-matter competence, balancing perspectives and avoiding monocultures; reviewer selection may consider geographic and career-stage diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written assessments with substantiated recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must provide written evaluations that justify their scientific judgements and include clear funding recommendations where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should state strengths/weaknesses, reference key literature or methodological concerns, and provide actionable feedback for applicants and decision bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel/committee decision-making and consensus-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rubric describing how review panels deliberate, weigh external reviews, and arrive at funding recommendations or rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels consider written reviews, hear applicants (where applicable), and document reasons for decisions; dissenting opinions may be recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of the review outcome and right to information
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards ensuring applicants receive reasoned decisions, summaries of reviews, and information on how decisions were reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision letters typically include review summaries and panel statements; applicants may have opportunities to respond to factual errors (right to be heard) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of proposals and review proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that proposal contents and review deliberations are treated confidentially to protect intellectual property and privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFG sets rules on data handling, limits on distribution of proposal material, and obligations for reviewers on confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance and procedural audits of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher-level standards to monitor, evaluate and improve the fairness, timeliness and effectiveness of DFG’s review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include performance indicators (e.g., time-to-decision), external audits, reviewer training, and mechanisms to handle complaints or appeals.
